resources.string: Optional. Recognises on this device whether a video is practice, education, news, entertainment and so on. Nothing leaves the device. It only ever adds warnings or ordering and never decides on its own; without the model ZenPipe works exactly as before.
Not available on this device (needs Android 7 and a 64-bit processor).
Not installed. The model download is not published yet.
Download the content recognition model (about %1$d MB) from GitHub? This is the only connection the content recognition ever makes; nothing about you or your videos is sent. Wi-Fi recommended.
Delete the content recognition model? ZenPipe then works as without it; you can download it again at any time.
No video classified yet. New feed videos are classified in the background after a feed refresh; opened videos with their description.

Latest classifications (newest first): categories with confidence · tone · feed weight · input (T = title and channel only, D = with description). Second line: strongest topics and formats. The recognition is wrong for about one video in seven.

The download does not change any switch. Once the model is installed, the two content switches in the list above take effect as they are set now: order the feed by content: %1$s, limit distressing videos: %2$s. Turning them off later is a loosening (24 hours); turning them off now, before the download, too.
Content recognition active. Order by content: %1$s, limit distressing videos: %2$s (Settings > Zen).
No effect yet: works only with the content recognition model.
Content recognition: order the feed by content (news and entertainment further back)
Content recognition: limit distressing videos (at most 1 in 10, never two in a row, not at the top)
The two content switches are in the list above. Turning them off is a loosening (takes effect after 24 hours). Without a working model the feed is ordered exactly as before.
To delete the model, first turn off both content switches above (a loosening that takes effect after 24 hours).
Content recognition: loading the newest videos …

The content recognition sees only %1$d of %2$d newer videos of \"%3$s\" as practice (follow-along, breathing, meditation, falling asleep). %4$d look like entertainment or news, e.g. \"%5$s\".\n\nThe recognition is wrong for about every fourth video. Practice videos are exempt from the feed limits and the mandatory pause. Please only mark channels and playlists you really use for practising.

The content recognition sees only %1$d of %2$d newer videos of \"%3$s\" as practice (follow-along, breathing, meditation, falling asleep).\n\nThe recognition is wrong for about every fourth video. Practice videos are exempt from the feed limits and the mandatory pause. Please only mark channels and playlists you really use for practising.
Clearly little practice: less than a third of the videos looks like practice.
%1$d of %2$d videos could not be loaded – judged by title and channel only.
%1$d of %2$d videos are for channel members only – judged by title and channel only.
not loadable, title and channel only
Content recognition: %1$d of %2$d newer videos look like practice – fits.
Content recognition: no clear picture (%1$d of %2$d videos without a category).
Content recognition not installed – no check.
Content recognition: the videos could not be loaded – no check.
Content recognition: only %1$d of %2$d newer videos look like practice (you chose to mark it anyway).

Channels or title keywords the content recognition should leave alone (e.g. a history channel read as politics, or \"good news\"): their videos keep their normal place in the feed and the limit for distressing videos does not apply. Adding is a loosening (takes effect after 24 hours), removing applies immediately.
Content recognition: exception for this channel
The content recognition will no longer push back %1$s from %2$s (in 24 hours); you can cancel it until then.
Zen settings are locked until %1$s. Adding an exception is a loosening and is possible again afterwards.
